title: Modulation of the AMPK/TFEB Axis by Ezetimibe Attenuates Neuroinflammatory, Oxidative Stress, and Neurotransmitter Dysregulation in Naloxone-precipitated Tramadol Withdrawal in Mice.
authors: Aditi; Wani, Shahid Nazir; Akanksha; Kumar, Amit; Singh, Varinder; Singh, Thakur Gurjeet; Grewal, Amarjot Kaur; Silakari, Pragati
journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究依折麦布通过AMPK/TFEB轴缓解曲马多戒断的神经炎症，仅含TFEB分子对接，非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，且无AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Tramadol withdrawal is associated with neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neurotransmitter imbalance, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Activation of the AMPK-TFEB (AMP-activated protein kinase-transcription factor EB) signaling axis enhances autophagy and cellular homeostasis and may mitigate withdrawal-associated neurotoxicity. To investigate whether ezetimibe attenuates naloxone-precipitated tramadol withdrawal in mice through modulation of the AMPK/TFEB pathway. Swiss albino mice received chronic tramadol exposure followed by naloxone to induce withdrawal. Ezetimibe (5 and 10 mg/kg, p.o.) was administered with or without the TFEB inhibitor eltrombopag. Behavioral outcomes (withdrawal severity score, jumping frequency, hyperalgesia), oxidative stress and inflammatory markers, neurotransmitter levels, and molecular docking interactions with TFEB were evaluated. Ezetimibe significantly reduced withdrawal severity, jumping frequency, hyperalgesia, lipid peroxidation, glutamate levels, and pro-inflammatory cytokines, while restoring antioxidant status, dopamine, and serotonin. Co-administration of eltrombopag attenuated these effects. Docking analysis revealed a stable interaction between ezetimibe and TFEB. Ezetimibe ameliorates tramadol-withdrawal-induced neurobehavioral and molecular alterations, most likely via AMPK-mediated activation of TFEB and enhancement of autophagy, highlighting its therapeutic potential in opioid withdrawal.
abstract_zh: 曲马多戒断与神经炎症、氧化应激及神经递质失衡相关，然而有效的治疗策略仍然有限。激活AMPK-TFEB（AMP活化蛋白激酶-转录因子EB）信号轴可增强自噬和细胞稳态，并可能减轻戒断相关的神经毒性。本研究旨在探讨依折麦布是否通过调节AMPK/TFEB通路减轻纳洛酮诱导的小鼠曲马多戒断反应。瑞士白化小鼠接受慢性曲马多暴露后给予纳洛酮以诱导戒断。依折麦布（5和10 mg/kg，口服）单独或与TFEB抑制剂艾曲泊帕联合给药。评估了行为学结果（戒断严重程度评分、跳跃频率、痛觉过敏）、氧化应激和炎症标志物、神经递质水平以及与TFEB的分子对接相互作用。依折麦布显著降低了戒断严重程度、跳跃频率、痛觉过敏、脂质过氧化、谷氨酸水平和促炎细胞因子，同时恢复了抗氧化状态、多巴胺和血清素。艾曲泊帕的联合给药减弱了这些效应。对接分析显示依折麦布与TFEB之间存在稳定的相互作用。依折麦布改善曲马多戒断诱导的神经行为学和分子改变，最可能通过AMPK介导的TFEB激活和自噬增强实现，凸显其在阿片类戒断中的治疗潜力。
